HomeEssentials Inc. - Q3 2024 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, everyone, and welcome to the HomeEssentials Inc. Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] Please also note, today's event is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, and thank you for joining us today to discuss HomeEssentials Inc.'s results for the Q3 2024. Joining me on today’s call are Mike Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Financial Officer; David Ramirez, Chief Merchandising Officer; Emily Patel, Chief Stores Officer; and Alex Rivera, Chief Marketing Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call contains forward-looking statements, which are subject to risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

With that, I’ll turn the call over to Mike Thompson.

Mike Thompson, Chief Executive Officer:
Thank you, Sarah. Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I’m pleased to report HomeEssentials Inc.'s performance for the Q3 2024. We continued to execute on our strategic priorities and delivered solid results despite the challenging macroeconomic environment.

Today I will cover seven key aspects of our performance:

1. Overall Performance: We posted consolidated revenues up 8.2% year-over-year to $2.8 billion with comparable store sales growth of 4.1%, reflecting disciplined execution across our 1,200-plus stores amid competition from big-box peers and e-commerce giants.

2. E-Commerce Growth: Digital channels now drive 22% of total sales, up from 17% last year, with strong omnichannel activation boosting in-store traffic.

3. Store Performance: Inventory discipline led to leaner levels down 7.5% YoY, supporting healthier turns and margins in our physical footprint.

4. Marketing Initiatives: Digital marketing delivered a 5.8x ROAS, efficiently acquiring customers and lifting traffic across channels.

5. Supply Chain Optimization: Advanced AI forecasting and vendor partnerships improved inventory turns to 5.1x, cutting days on hand significantly.

6. Loyalty Program Update: Our program with 28 million members enhanced repeat rates to 62% for engaged households through personalized engagement.

7. Sustainability Initiatives: Optimization efforts reduced waste by 30%, aligning with ESG goals while preserving value recovery.

We are confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Lisa Chen to provide more details on our financial results.

Lisa Chen, Chief Financial Officer:
Thank you, Mike. Good morning. I'll provide a more detailed review of our financial performance for the Q3 2024.

Revenue: Our total revenue for the quarter was $2.8 billion, an 8.2% increase compared to the same period last year.

Gross Margin: Gross margin was 38.2%, primarily driven by lower markdowns, improved inventory productivity, and favorable product costs from vendor negotiations.

Operating Expenses: Operating expenses were $1.23 billion, representing 43.9% of revenue.

Net Income: Net income was $285 million, or $1.18 per share.

Cash Flow: We generated $420 million in cash flow from operations.

Inventory: Inventory levels are currently down 7.5% year-over-year to $2.82 billion, with turns improving to 5.1x.

We are maintaining a strong balance sheet and are well positioned to invest in our growth initiatives.

To give you deeper insight into these results, let me dive into digital marketing effectiveness, one of our key growth levers in the brick-and-mortar space where we compete with players like Amazon, Wayfair, Target, and Lowe's. Our digital efforts bridge our 1,200-plus physical stores to the $150 billion U.S. home goods e-commerce market. We've turned digital into a high-ROI engine, with digital touchpoints contributing 22% of total sales this quarter, up from 17% a year ago, while driving 35% of in-store traffic via omnichannel like BOPIS.

Total digital marketing spend was $145 million, up 15% YoY, or 5.2% of revenues—more efficient than the 7-8% industry average for peers like Macy's. This yielded a blended ROAS of 5.8x, up from 4.7x, beating our 5x target and generating $420 million in attributable sales. CAC dropped 12% to $22.50 per new customer, with CLV to CAC at 4.2x from 3.5x.

By channel, paid search took 42% of spend at $61 million, with Google Ads and Bing Shopping at 7.2x ROAS from Performance Max campaigns on queries like "kitchen remodel appliances near me," lifting AOV 11% to $185 via dynamic remarketing upsells. Social media, 28% or $40 million, hit 4.9x ROAS; Meta drove engagement among 25-44-year-olds, while TikTok's 15% budget share exploded at 6.1x ROAS on #HomeRefresh challenges, acquiring 1.2 million users at $14 CAC with shoppable UGC boosting conversions 24%.

Owned channels like email and SMS, 18% of spend, achieved 9.2x ROAS via Klaviyo on our CDP, with 42% open rates on personalized flows driving $85 million in lapsed customer reactivation and repeat rates to 62%. Display and programmatic, 12%, delivered 4.2x ROAS via The Trade Desk, shifting 30% to clean rooms for privacy compliance.

Omnichannel trends show 68% online-to-offline conversions: 42% of digital ad clicks to BOPIS within 7 days, 26 to store visits. GeoLift tests confirmed digital lifts physical comps by 2.7 points. Regionally, Northeast (320 stores) saw 41% traffic from digital at 6.5x ROAS; Southeast grew social 32% YoY at 7x TikTok ROAS; rural Midwest focuses on local SEO up 19%.

Tech-wise, Vertex AI personalizes 1,200 micro-audiences from our 28 million loyalty app members (up 14%), lifting ROAS 31%; Meridian MTA credits upper-funnel like YouTube (8% spend). Ahead, 40% budgets to contextual/first-party by Q1 2025, CTV pilots at 3x ROAS, Shopify/Criteo for $12 million retail media revenue, zero-party data at 72% consent. Even in 2% comp decline, digital keeps marketing margins at 28%, supporting 12-15% EPS growth.

Next, our strategies for inventory optimization have turned a potential drag into a competitive advantage amid omnichannel pressures and supply headwinds. Entering the year, turns were 4.2x with 87 DOH; now at 5.1x turns and 71 DOH, aiding 150 bps gross margin expansion, markdowns down 18% to 4.2% of sales, WOS to 10 weeks on apparel, GMROI up 15% to 2.8x.

First, AI demand sensing via Blue Yonder integrates POS, loyalty (25 million members), Placer.ai traffic, weather, macros—92% accuracy vs. 78%, cutting stockouts 35%, overstocks 22% in activewear, saving $45 million in markdowns. Northeast/Midwest DOH down 20%; Europe to 74 days; Asia-Pacific comps +12%.

Second, omnichannel orchestration with Manhattan WMS and 85% RFID high-velocity SKUs; ship-from-store 28% of e-com (down last-mile 22%), BOPIS 18% digital. 12 micro-fulfillment centers cut WOS 40% on beauty; IoT for 95% planogram adherence.

Third, VMI for 35% OTB with P&G, Levi's, Unilever—JIT cuts safety stock 25%, dynamic OTB favors home goods. Sustainability: 30% less textile waste, 85% recovery on slow-movers. Narrowed SKUs 12% in basics, 98% holiday sell-through.

Ahead, turns to 5.4x, DOH 68 days, $75 million RFID/GenAI capex.

Building on that, our inventory levels year-over-year underscore this discipline. At quarter-end, consolidated inventory was $2.82 billion, down 7.5% from $3.05 billion last year—third straight quarter of reduction, leanest since 2019. Comp store basis, down 9.2%, excluding 15 new stores and 22 closures.

By segment: Apparel/softlines down 12.4% to $1.1 billion, WOS to 8.2 weeks avoiding markdowns; home/hardlines up 2.1% to $850 million at 11.5 turns; electronics flat at $870 million post-SKU cuts.

Full-year turns 8.7x, up 12%, WOS 12.1 weeks below benchmarks. Sunbelt down 11% at 9.4x turns; Northeast/Midwest down 5% at 7.9x; West down 8.5%.

Blue Yonder Phase 2 at 92% forecast accuracy cut excess $180 million; RFID 75% apparel slashes shrink 15%; VMI 60% core volume frees $250 million working capital. Target: under 60-day dwell for 80% SKUs. Q1 down another 4-6% YoY.

On markdown activity's margin effect: Markdowns were 11.8% of sales, up 140 bps YoY, creating 90 bps headwind to 37.9% gross margin—still above target and peers. 60% from apparel/home seasonal clearance amid excess spring intake, depth 52%; hardlines 25% volume shaved 30 bps.

Ex-markdown, margins up 20 bps from 1.5% lower costs, owned labels 42% sales. Shrink stable 1.6%. $185 million lost profit. Sunbelt 9.5%; Northeast/Midwest 14.2%; Canada 13.1%; Europe 8.7%.

Trending down from 14.2% Q4 peak with 12.1 WOS, 5.8x turns. Q3 guide 12-12.5%. AI pricing in 60% stores lifts turns 15%, margins 25 bps; RFID 92% top stores; vendor scorecards cut risk 10%. Right-sizing SKUs 12%, omnichannel absorbs 22% clearance at full price. Margins trough Q3 37.5-38%, expand Q4.

Shifting to omnichannel progress: Digital sales 28% revenue, up to $1.2 billion +32% YoY; 62% fulfilled via stores (up 15 pts), costs 4.2% vs. 12-15% pure e-comm.

BOPIS 41% digital orders (vs. 35% industry), 2.8 million transactions +48%, $850 million at $145 AOV with app upsells, 95% conversion. Curbside +55% to 1.1 million, 22% fulfillment, 31% Sunbelt penetration, under 8 min fulfillment via StoreFlow OMS/Zebra.

$150 million tech: Manhattan WMS 98% visibility; Klaviyo app DAUs 4.2 million +37%; RFID pilots cut errors 40%. Midwest/Southeast traffic +22%; West +25%. Omnichannel margins 42.5% +450 bps, retention 78%. Q3 BOPIS+ subscription, ship-from-store 75%; 65% digital fulfillment FYE.

For key assumptions underlying guidance: FY2024 comps 1.5-3.5%, adj EPS $2.85-3.15, op margins +20-50 bps. Q4 comps 2-4%, traffic mid-single, units soft; 1-2% weather drag. Sunbelt +150 bps; Northeast flat; Canada/Mexico 4-6%.

Gross margin +75 bps to 38.5-39% from freight deleveraging, RFID shrink cuts, flat EDLP. SG&A delever 50-75 bps to 24.5% via AI scheduling (OT -10%), wage 3.5%; capex $450 million, 60% remodels/BOPIS. Confidence 95-105, unemployment 4.2%; loyalty ramp 12-15%. Stores of Future pilots, dual-sourcing. Upside tariffs relief; downside grocery deflation.

On financial outlook: Q4 sales $2.45-2.55 billion +2-5%, comps flat-+2% (stores +1-+3%, e-comm -2-flat), BOPIS 28%. Gross 38.5-39.5% +100 bps, shrink -15%. SG&A 26.5-27.5%; op income $280-320 million, EPS $1.05-1.20. FY2024 sales $9.8-10.0 billion comps +1.5-+3%, EPS $4.20-4.40, FCF $650-750 million. Sunbelt +5-+7%; Northeast flat--1%; Canada/Mexico +3%. Capex $450 million DCs/remodels. Hedged liquidity $1.2 billion.

We are well positioned. Now, I'd like to hand it over to David Ramirez, our Chief Merchandising Officer, to discuss our new product lines, followed by Emily Patel to discuss store operations, and then Alex Rivera to discuss marketing initiatives.

David Ramirez, Chief Merchandising Officer:
Thank you, Lisa. This quarter, we launched our EcoHome sustainable line, which has seen strong uptake with 25% unit growth and higher full-price sell-through, contributing to better GMROI. We are excited about the potential of this new product and other upcoming launches in owned brands.

Emily Patel, Chief Stores Officer:
Thank you, David. We continue to focus on improving the customer experience in our stores. We have implemented dedicated BOPIS and curbside stations with RFID-enabled picking and are seeing positive results, including 22% traffic uplift and higher conversion in pilot locations.

Alex Rivera, Chief Marketing Officer:
Thank you, Emily. Our new marketing campaign, Home Refresh, has increased brand awareness by 25%, leveraging TikTok challenges and personalized email flows to drive both digital and in-store engagement.

Now, let's open the line for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith (Goldman Sachs):
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the impact of inflation on your sales?

Mike Thompson, Chief Executive Officer:
Good morning, John. Inflation at 4.1% on durables has squeezed discretionary spend, but our value tier at 45% of sales and digital efficiencies like 2.7-point comp lift from omnichannel have helped us maintain 4.1% overall comps. We're stress-testing scenarios and focused on essentials and owned labels for resilience.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mary Johnson with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Mary Johnson (JPMorgan):
What are your expectations for same-store sales growth in the next quarter?

Lisa Chen, Chief Financial Officer:
Thanks, Mary. For Q4, we're guiding comps flat to +2%, with stores +1% to +3% on mid-single-digit traffic from BOPIS and remodels, offset by e-comm lapping tough comps. Sunbelt strength at +5-7% balances softer Northeast.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Bob Lee with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Bob Lee (Morgan Stanley):
Can you elaborate on the supply chain improvements?

Mike Thompson, Chief Executive Officer:
Absolutely, Bob. Our AI forecasting with Blue Yonder at 92% accuracy, VMI for 35% OTB, and micro-fulfillment have cut DOH to 71 days and Red Sea impacts via dual-sourcing. This freed $250 million working capital while keeping holiday assortments intact.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Anna Kim with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Anna Kim (Barclays):
What is the impact from the loyalty program?

Mike Thompson, Chief Executive Officer:
Great question, Anna. With 28 million members up 14%, loyalty drives 62% repeat rates via personalized Klaviyo flows, contributing $85 million in reactivations and 200 bps wallet share. It's core to our 4.2x CLV:CAC and omnichannel retention at 78%.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Chris Patel with Citi. Please go ahead.

Chris Patel (Citi):
Can you expand on omnichannel progress and digital ROAS sustainability?

Alex Rivera, Chief Marketing Officer:
Hi Chris. Omnichannel hit 62% store fulfillment, BOPIS 41% digital at $145 AOV, curbside +55%, margins 42.5%. ROAS 5.8x is sustainable with AI personalization, CTV pilots at 3x, and first-party data shifts—positioning us for cookieless future while blending store tactile appeal.

Operator:
Thank you. That concludes today's questions.

Mike Thompson, Chief Executive Officer:
Thank you for your questions. In closing, we are pleased with our progress this quarter and remain focused on executing our long-term strategy. Thank you for your continued support.

Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations:
This concludes today's call. Thank you for joining us.
